title: Challenger, Pad 39B, 28 January 1986: launch-morning reconstruction (Unreal Engine renders)
scene: Launch morning before liftoff; sun for 11:38 EST (elevation 41.1 deg, azimuth 161.5 deg). No launch, no breakup and nothing after T+73 s; no after-the-inquiry views.
engine: Unreal Engine 5.8, real-time scene rendered offline frame by frame; no AI image generation
coordinates: north_m / east_m from the stack (flame-trench axis); heights as stated in each caption

files.title: Press site distance
estimated: NOT the press site: the real press site is about 5.6 km south-west, which is lagoon and marsh in this terrain, so this is a similar distance (5.4 km) on the nearest broad dry ground, south-east of the pad
at this range the stack is only a few pixels wide in the 360 view; the clip uses a telephoto view
the bare raised mound left of the pad in the clip is most likely the Pad 39A hardstand from the 2018 lidar; no 39A structures are modelled
structure positions and sizes are proportioned from NASA photographs (estimates)
files.caption: Press site distance: at press-site distance on the coastal strip, looking north-west along the coast to the pad; 5.4 km south-east of the stack, eye height 1.7 m above the ground on the barrier island.

files.title: Walkthrough: fence to white room
files.caption: On foot from the south gate in the perimeter fence (about 310 m south of the stack, eye height 1.7 m) up the crawlerway and across the pad apron to the foot of the Fixed Service Structure, then at the 147 ft level out along the crew access arm to the white room beside the orbiter hatch.
estimated: the lift ride up the tower is not shown: a slow dissolve takes the camera from the foot of the tower to the arm
slow dissolves also shorten the walk (fence gate to crawlerway top, crawlerway top to the apron)
on the arm the camera keeps to its south side, where the estimated cross braces are at knee height
structure positions and sizes are proportioned from NASA photographs (estimates)
